passages.P7: Those circulating a cropped screenshot are falsely claiming that The Wire referred to Durga Puja as 'racist' and called the Hindu goddess a 'sex worker'.
passages.P8: Minister of minority affairs Smriti Irani. Photo: PTI
passages.P10: **New Delhi:** As India celebrates the festivals of Durga Puja and Navratri, a cropped screenshot of a 2016 article by *The Wire* is being misrepresented and doing the rounds on social media, falsely claiming the news website referred to the festival as "racist" and called the Hindu goddess a "sex worker".
passages.P11:
> First #Tanishq then #EROS\_NOW and now #TheWire Hope some day they also get some guts to write something about the 6 year old girl Aisha.. It's easy to target Hinduism as you know that you'll not be beheaded after writing this. #TheWire #DurgaPuja #sicularism #sickularism pic.twitter.com/LKaLm8zl6z
>
> — James vinchi 🇮🇳 (@JamesVinchi) October 23, 2020
passages.P12: The text in the viral screenshot reads: "Durga Puja is the most controversial racial festival, where a fair skinned beautiful goddess Durga is depicted brutally killing a dark-skinned native called Mahishasura. Mahishasura, a brave self-respecting leader, was tricked into marriage by the Aryans. They hired a sex worker called Durga, who enticed Mahishasura into marriage and killed him after nine nights of honeymooning, during sleep."
passages.P13: The screenshot is taken from *The Wire's* news article *Mahishasura and the Minister* dated February 27, 2016, quoting Union minister Smriti Irani who read the aforementioned lines about Durga Puja in her Lok Sabha speech. According to the article, Irani was reading the description of Durga Puja from a pamphlet allegedly distributed by the organisers of the event when students of Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) celebrated 'Mahishasur Martyrdom Day.'
passages.P14: Fact-checking website *Boomlive* reported this story earlier on Monday and quoted founding editor of *The Wire* Siddharth Varadarajan who explained on Twitter that the screenshot is a "quote of Smriti Irani, as HRD min in Feb 2016, reading out in parliament extracts from what she said was a JNU pamphlet."
passages.P16:
> What‘s being circulated by Hindutva loonies on Twitter as The Wire’s ‘view’ is actually a quote of Smriti Irani, as HRD min in Feb 2016, reading out in parliament extracts from what she said was a JNU pamphlet. The full story we ran is here: https://t.co/Rqf0qWljIo
>
> — Siddharth (@svaradarajan) October 26, 2020
passages.P17: The same speech is available on the official YouTube channel of the Bharatiya Janata Party.
passages.P19: *This article was originally published on* Boom Live.
passages.P21: This article went live on October twenty-sixth, two thousand twenty, at twenty-one minutes past six in the evening.
passages.P22: *The Wire is now on WhatsApp. Follow our channel for sharp analysis and opinions on the latest developments.*

records.title: The Wire did not 'disrespect' Durga; excerpt from 2016 article ...
records.retrieval_query: Did The Wire publish any article, column, or social media post that described Durga puja as racist, and if so, what was the exact wording, author, and date?

passages.P3: An excerpt from an article in The Wire is making the rounds on Twitter to claim that the news organisation promoted ‘anti-Hindu’ sentiments by terming Durga Puja a “racist festival” and the Hindu deity a “sex worker”.
passages.P4: Ex-navy officer Harinder Sikka questioned The Wire in a critically worded tweet, “Can u dare write such obscene words for Islam?”
passages.P5: Twitter handle @missionkaali followed by Delhi BJP leader Kapil Mishra also shared the screenshot speculating if the outlet indeed published the excerpt.
passages.P6:
Several other users — @Voice\_Of\_Dharma, @Muralik79739498 — posted the screenshot. Twitter handle @indianrightwing opined, “Maa durga being called a s\*x worker that too during navratri by  
@thewire\_in. There can be no punishment except for legal death sentence…”
passages.P9: Twitter handle @indianrightwing which suggested the “death penalty” for The Wire as punishment for alleged “Hinduphobic” views also shared the article containing the excerpt in question. Had the user read the report, they’d know that the news organisation wasn’t promoting its own opinions but a reference made by Union Minister Smriti Irani in 2016. The use of direct quotes itself hints that the statement was not made by The Wire.
passages.P10: The article dates back to February 27, 2016, after the former HRD Minister’s Lok Sabha speech addressing the criticism of the government’s handling of the protests at JNU by alleging that “anti-national” events were held on campus. She made the speech on February 24, 2016, and the relevant portion can be watched 31:40 minutes onward.
passages.P11: Irani claimed that the excerpt on Durga Puja was printed on a pamphlet for the celebrations of the ‘Mahishasur Martyrdom Day’ in 2014 which was denied by the organisers of the event. JNU student Anil, a member of All India Backward Students’ Forum (AIBSF), who was one of the organisers, told The Wire, “What Irani said was totally fabricated. The things she said we wrote in our pamphlet were in fact from an ABVP pamphlet, where they claimed to be quoting what we had said. But she is making it sound like we said it. The JNU administration may have given her the pamphlets, but that does not make them ‘certified’. They simply collect them.”
passages.P12: However, JNU administration claimed that the document quoted in the Parliament was authentic. “The HRD ministry had asked us to authenticate the documents including pamphlets of the events. We checked the security reports in our records and the pamphlets were found included in them. The documents were correct according to our records and the same has been conveyed to the ministry,” JNU Registrar Bhupinder Zutshi told PTI.
passages.P13: A controversy erupted as AIBSF intended to hold an event to show the sharp contrast of Mahalaya celebrations for several Dalit and tribal communities with Durga Puja festivities. The event has sparked controversy in the past as well. Bahujan community rejects the Brahmanical representation of Mahisa-Durga by mourning the death of their king who is slain by goddess Durga to reflect the triumph of good over evil.

records.title: No, The Wire Didn't Publish an Excerpt Against Goddess Durga
records.retrieval_query: Did The Wire publish any article, column, or social media post that described the goddess Durga as a sex worker, and if so, what was the exact wording, author, and date?

passages.P2: # No, The Wire Didn’t Publish an Excerpt Against Goddess Durga
passages.P3: ## The viral excerpt is from a pamphlet read by Union Minister Smriti Irani in the Parliament.
passages.P15: An excerpt from a report by The Wire is doing the rounds on social media to claim that the news portal intentionally disrespected Hindu goddess Durga by calling her a “sex slave”.
passages.P16: However, it is noteworthy that the excerpt has been taken out of context. It is from a report where The Wire had quoted Union Minister Smriti Irani speaking in the Parliament and reading out a pamphlet insulting the Hindu festival of Durga Puja which she claimed was distributed on the campus of the Jawaharlal Nehru University.
passages.P18: The viral screenshot which is being massively shared on Twitter reads: “Durga Puja is the most controversial racial festival, where a fair-skinned beautiful goddess Durga is depicted brutally killing a dark-skinned native called Mahishasura. Mahishasura, a brave self-respecting leader, was tricked into marriage by the Aryans. They hired a sex worker called Durga, who enticed Mahishasura into marriage and killed him after nine nights of honeymooning, during sleep”.
passages.P20: Among those who shared this screenshot and attributed the quote to The Wire is former Navy officer and author Harinder Sikka.
passages.P22: A keyword search using the terms from viral excerpt directed us to the full report published on The Wire. Titled “**Mahishasura and the Minister**” the report by Jahnavi Sen talks about Smriti Irani’s speech in the Lok Sabha as the then HRD minister.
passages.P23: According to the report, Irani while responding to the criticism of the government over its handling of the events at JNU stated that “anti-national” events had taken place at the campus.
passages.P24: The Wire’s report then quotes the minister as she read from a pamphlet which she claimed was distributed on the campus.
passages.P25: “Durga Puja is the most controversial racial festival, where a fair-skinned beautiful goddess Durga is depicted brutally killing a dark-skinned native called Mahishasura. Mahishasura, a brave self-respecting leader, was tricked into marriage by the Aryans. They hired a sex worker called Durga, who enticed Mahishasura into marriage and killed him after nine nights of honeymooning, during sleep,” the portal quoted her as saying.
passages.P26: This explainer by **The Quint** details the entire controversy as it happened in the Parliament.
passages.P27: Clearly, an excerpt from a pamphlet which was read by Smriti Irani in the Parliament and was subsequently reported by The Wire is now being used without context to claim that the news portal is “anti-Hindu” and “anti-national”.
passages.P28: Siddharth Varadarajan, founding editor of The Wire, himself shared a link of the original article on Twitter.

>
> — Siddharth (@svaradarajan) October 26, 2020
